g.text: ADR-007: What the public sees, and what only staff see
Which data does TrialWatch show to anyone, and which only to its admins and moderators, now that the web interface can be served to the
what forces this decision now: facts and constraints, no solutions
• ADR-006 let anyone browse every page: unreviewed model judgements, their traces (prompts, raw answers), sources and transfers, gold labels with false-
accusation flags, and staff emails in the history.
• A judgement says a sponsor did not report fully: public, it is an accusation. A model can misread a page, so a wrong one harms a sponsor and our
• The methodology should stay open: how we check (requirement sets, prompts, run settings) is what makes a result trustworthy.
• Staff are people: their emails are personal data and nobody outside needs them.
• ADR-001 proposed manual approval below 99% confidence; we have no calibrated confidence yet.
2–3 real options; the current proposal is only one of them
How it works: all pages stay open; unreviewed
– a draft accusation is still public and indexed
B. Publish step and a staff view
How it works: checks.publication records which
deleted). A run publishes one by itself when
judgements of its kind agreed with gold labels ≥
90% of the time over ≥ 20 items; the rest wait
for a person. The public sees the newest
published judgement with its answers and
verified quotes; staff also see drafts, traces,
+ nothing reaches the public unmeasured or
– reviews wait until gold covers a kind
How it works: a viewer role; nothing is public.
– accounts to manage for every reader
+ better · 0 no difference · – worse, and a few words why
0 one table, page filters, a review
Undo: how hard to reverse later
what we chose and which criteria decided it
We choose B. Public: trials, sponsors and their documents (files a source gave, or a person's upload once a published judgement quotes it), the newest
published judgement per trial with each answer's verified quote, how it was published, and a marker when its documents changed since; runs, prompts,
requirement sets, and history with people shown as "TrialWatch staff". Staff only (view.internal): unpublished judgements, traces and raw answers, sources
and transfers, gold, run tallies, the workflow and /review, and names. Confidence is measured, not asked: a judgement's kind (model, prompt text,
requirement set, label, quotes verified, asked again with every page, a question unanswered) is compared with gold labels; at ≥ 90% agreement over ≥ 20
items a run publishes it as it finishes, any label, recording the share and its basis (checks/publishing.py). Below that, too few items, or undecided: a
moderator or admin publishes it (judgement.publish). Decided by harm and openness.
Easier: serving the site publicly; reviewing is one button on the trial
page, and every publication and withdrawal is audited.
Harder: until gold covers a kind, a person reviews every result; a
changed prompt or model starts a new kind with no measurement.
Revisit when: gold grows enough to lower MIN_GOLD_ITEMS or tune the 90%
line; sponsors should see drafts before publication; a public API or
Lab: tests/test_publication.py (drafts hidden, published shown without the
trace, withdrawal, staff-only pages, names, files) and test_publishing.py
(90% line, too few items, accusations, a new prompt is a new kind).
Decided with the user on 2026-11-21: the public is anyone; the public sees verdict and quotes, not the trace; gold and sources are staff only; runs,
prompts and history stay public. Then: approve by hand below 90% confidence, measured on gold; above it any label, accusations included, publishes by
How to use: copy to docs/adr/ADR-NNN-name.excalidraw · replace the grey text (set it to black) · status chip colour: orange open, yellow proposed, green accepted, grey
superseded · one page: if it doesn't fit, the decision is too big, so split it.
